Purpose To examine heat exposure at work and home and the work–recovery cycle and temporal variation of kidney strain, muscle injury and inflammation biomarkers in sugarcane workers. Methods 20 male sugarcane workers (age: 33 ± 7 years) with a workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention were observed over 4 days, at the end (18 h post-shift recovery) and beginning of a work week (42 h post-shift recovery). Measures included work intensity (heart rate), gastro-intestinal temperature, estimated body core temperature (using heart rate), fluid consumption, pre- and post-work blood and urine samples, physical activity (accelerometery) away from work, plus ambient heat exposure at work and home. Results On workdays, workers awakened at approx. 02:40 after 5 h sleep in ~ 30 °C. Across work shifts, daily average WBGT ranged from 26 to 29 °C (cooler than normal) and average workload intensity ranged from 55 to 58%HR max . Workers reported consuming ~ 8 L of water and ~ 4 × 300 mL bags of electrolyte fluid each day. Serum creatinine, cystatin C and creatine phosphokinase markedly increased post-work and decreased during recovery; serum potassium did the opposite (all p < 0.01). Biomarker concentration changes were similar between recovery periods (18 h vs. 42 h; all p > 0.27). C-reactive protein was the highest at the end of the work week ( p = 0.01). Conclusion Despite RSH intervention, cross-shift kidney strain was marked (recovering overnight) and systemic inflammation increased over the work week. Thus, biomonitoring of kidney function in occupational populations should be performed before a work shift at any point in the work week. This is essential knowledge for field studies and surveillance. Supplementary Information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s00421-024-05610-3. German Investment Corporation F0877/SAP3705 Glaser Jason http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/501100004343 Stavros Niarchos Foundation GL 2016 Glaser Jason issue-copyright-statement © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2025 Introduction In recent decades, outbreaks of chronic kidney disease of non-traditional origin (CKDnt) have emerged globally at epidemic rates in Mesoamerica, Sri Lanka, India, and other regions (Wesseling et al. 2020 ; Glaser et al. 2016 ). In Mesoamerica, CKDnt has been characterized as an occupational disease driven by heat stress from strenuous manual labor performed in hot environments (Wesseling et al. 2020 ). Subsequently, it has been postulated that episodes of acute kidney injury (AKI) or kidney strain, due to repeat occupational heat exposure, cause chronic functional and structural kidney damage that develops into CKDnt (Hansson et al. 2020 ; Chawla and Kimmel 2012 ). Indeed, workforces at high risk of developing CKDnt show a decline in kidney function across work shifts (Butler-Dawson et al. 2019 ; Santos et al. 2015 ; García-Trabanino et al. 2015 ; Wesseling et al. 2016 ; Sorensen et al. 2019 ) and across harvest seasons (Kupferman et al. 2018 ; Hansson et al. 2019b , 2020 ; Wesseling et al. 2016 ). Furthermore, cross-shift changes in kidney function (as measured via serum creatinine) over a week have been shown to forecast end-of-harvest kidney function in sugarcane workers (Dally et al. 2020 ). Thus, following an acute insult, insufficient restoration of the kidney to normal morphology and function may lead to permanent damage and CKD (Lameire et al. 2013 ). Added to this, C-reactive protein (CRP, a sensitive biomarker of inflammation) has been shown to increase among sugarcane workers performing the physically most demanding tasks during the harvest season, especially in those developing kidney injury (Hansson et al. 2020 , 2019a ). Whether CRP dynamics across the working week signal an occupation-induced pro-inflammatory state in sugarcane workers has not been previously explored. The importance of recovery in the possible pathogenesis of CKDnt has been outlined by Hansson et al. ( 2020 ) and shares many parallels with the ‘overtraining syndrome’ in athletes, where a maladaptive inflammatory response develops due to frequent exposure to exercise-induced physiological strain and insufficient recovery (Kreher and Schwartz 2012 ; Armstrong et al. 2022 ). Notably, heat stroke/illness can also trigger the overtraining syndrome (Kreher and Schwartz 2012 ). The nature of industrial agricultural sugarcane work in Mesoamerica is that it is repetitive and physically very strenuous (Lucas et al. 2022 , 2015 ). During a harvest season, workers can work between 5 to 11 h/day and 6 to 7 days a week, for 5 to 6 months. Thus, workers’ opportunity for recuperative rest is limited and likely insufficient. Added to this, organizational factors such as the piece rate payment system, used throughout industrial agriculture, incentivizes workers to work harder, inhibiting their opportunity or willingness to take rest breaks and recover during work shifts (Mitchell et al. 2018 ; Spector et al. 2015 ). Additionally, workers often have other tasks they undertake after a work shift, such as subsistence farming or a second job (Raines et al. 2014 ), which further limits their rest and recovery. Workers’ physical activity, sleep patterns and ambient living temperatures away from work have not been described. Yet, recovery may be a crucial factor in the development of CKDnt among agricultural workers. The aim of the present study was to assess cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery of kidney function and muscle injury biomarkers, assess the inflammatory response to a working week, and to characterize the work and home environment (including workers’ physical activity, sleep patterns and ambient living temperatures away from work) to understand the context of this work–recovery cycle. Therefore, the recovery of kidney function and muscle injury biomarkers after one night’s recovery from a work shift (at the end of a working week), compared to two nights and one day’s recovery (at the beginning of a working week, after a day off) was explored. Moreover, a better understanding of the short-term temporal variation in biomarkers of kidney function (i.e., kidney strain) is also needed to inform field study and health surveillance protocols in occupational settings (Fig. 1 ).

extracted_data.document_summary: This observational study investigated the work-recovery cycle and temporal variation of kidney strain, muscle injury, hydration, and inflammation biomarkers in 20 male sugarcane workers exposed to repeat heat stress and strenuous manual labor, despite a workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. It assessed biomarker dynamics across work shifts and different recovery periods (18h vs 42h post-shift). The study found marked cross-shift kidney and muscle strain, alongside an accumulation of systemic inflammation over the work week, with recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers being similar for both recovery durations. The findings highlight the importance of biomonitoring for occupational populations.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study investigated the impact of occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor, specifically sugarcane cutting, on worker health, with an applied workplace Rest.Shade.Hydration (RSH) intervention. This intervention included a maximum six-hour workday, hourly mandated rest breaks in the shade, easy access to cool water, and electrolyte solutions (300 mL bolis/bags containing sugar, sodium chloride, and potassium phosphate).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: 20 male sugarcane workers were observed over 4 days, covering work shifts and recovery periods (18h and 42h post-shift). Workload intensity ranged from 55-58%HR max, with daily average Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) between 26-29 °C, which was considered cooler than normal for a harvest period. Workers consumed approximately 8 L of water and four 300 mL electrolyte bags daily. Work shifts averaged around 5 hours, with Monday shifts showing higher workload intensity and heat stress. Recovery rates for kidney and muscle injury biomarkers were found to be similar between 18 hours and 42 hours of rest (p > 0.27), indicating no significant difference in recovery duration comparison within this timeframe.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01). Cross-shift changes were similar to previously reported values, showing worsening pre-shift levels over a work week. Changes were similar between 18 h vs. 42 h recovery (p > 0.27).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism, filtered and excreted by the kidneys; used as a marker for kidney glomerular filtration and function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery following occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting) in a weekly work-rest cycle, despite RSH intervention.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates daily kidney strain, recovery capacity, and can reflect hydration status or muscle breakdown. Worsening pre-shift levels suggest a decline in kidney function and can forecast end-of-harvest kidney function. Biomonitoring is advised before a work shift.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01). Cross-shift increases were more pronounced than creatinine, especially during Monday shifts (p = 0.02), and similar between 18 h vs. 42 h recovery (p > 0.27).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A sensitive protein marker for kidney glomerular filtration, independent of diet, muscle, and physical activity, synthesized at a constant rate.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery following occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting) in a weekly work-rest cycle, despite RSH intervention.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates daily kidney strain and acute kidney stress. It is a valuable cross-shift and cross-harvest marker of kidney strain, particularly useful due to its independence from muscle catabolism. Biomonitoring is advised before a work shift.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Markedly increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01). Changes were similar between 18 h vs. 42 h recovery (p > 0.27), although one report indicated a larger decrease during longer rest (p = 0.01) after excluding an outlier.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enzyme primarily found in muscle cells; its release into the bloodstream indicates muscle damage and is involved in energy metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery following occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting) in a weekly work-rest cycle, despite RSH intervention. Associated with acute kidney injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage, physiological stress, and recovery capacity. Episodes of muscle injury leading to myoglobinuria and kidney inflammation are a potential driver of AKI and CKD.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Consistently higher at the end of the work week (Saturday) compared to the beginning (Monday; p = 0.01), indicating accumulating low-grade inflammation. Levels peak 24-48 hours after stimuli, making cross-shift analysis less meaningful.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Sensitive acute-phase protein biomarker of systemic inflammation, synthesized by the liver.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Accumulating during the working week of occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting), despite RSH intervention.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an occupation-induced pro-inflammatory state and accumulated physiological stress over the working week, hypothesized to contribute to CKDnt. Biomonitoring of inflammation is important for occupational health.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased during work shifts and increased during recovery periods (p < 0.01), showing an opposite pattern to kidney and muscle damage markers. Post-shift levels were sometimes at the lower reference interval limits (3.5 mmol/L). Changes were similar between 18 h vs. 42 h recovery (p > 0.27). Diurnal variation and rapid re-entry into skeletal muscle post-exercise are noted influences.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A crucial electrolyte for nerve and muscle cell function, involved in maintaining cellular fluid and electrolyte balance, and kidney regulation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Cross-shift changes and post-shift recovery following occupational heat exposure and strenuous manual labor (sugarcane cutting), influenced by diurnal variation, rapid muscle re-entry, and electrolyte-containing fluid intake, despite RSH intervention.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates electrolyte balance and physiological response to physical exertion. Imbalance can be linked to kidney strain or muscle activity; maintaining homeostasis is critical for health.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (during work shifts) and lower (during recovery)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased during work shifts and decreased during recovery periods (p < 0.01), with greater increases observed during Monday work shifts (p < 0.01).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Major plasma protein involved in maintaining osmotic pressure and transporting various substances; also an indicator of systemic stress or hydration status.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Work shifts, particularly Monday work shifts, and recovery periods in sugarcane workers under physical workload and heat stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Can reflect hydration status through hemoconcentration during work shifts and indicates systemic physiological response to acute exertion.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: mostly stable, with some instances of lower (mild hyponatremia)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels remained mostly stable across work shifts, with some post-shift samples indicating mild hyponatremia (134–136 mmol/L) or being at the lower reference interval limits (135 mmol/L). No clear work-recovery dynamic was observed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A major extracellular electrolyte vital for fluid balance, nerve impulse transmission, and muscle contraction, essential for electrolyte homeostasis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Across work shifts and recovery periods during strenuous sugarcane cutting with high fluid intake, despite RSH intervention.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates maintenance of electrolyte homeostasis. While generally stable, instances of mild hyponatremia suggest risks associated with both inadequate and excessive water intake during occupational heat exposure.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A product of purine metabolism; acts as an antioxidant, but high levels can indicate cell breakdown or kidney dysfunction.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Work shifts and recovery periods in sugarcane workers under physical workload and heat stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Did not serve as a clear indicator of physiological changes during work-recovery cycles in this context.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The main nitrogenous waste product of protein metabolism, primarily excreted by the kidneys; reflects protein catabolism and kidney function/hydration.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Work shifts and recovery periods in sugarcane workers under physical workload and heat stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Did not serve as a clear indicator of physiological changes during work-recovery cycles in this context.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Levels were uniformly undetectable or very low.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A major plasma protein; its presence in urine in significant amounts typically indicates kidney damage (impaired filtration).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Throughout work and recovery periods in sugarcane workers under physical workload and heat stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates healthy kidney filtration function, suggesting no significant kidney damage or pathology resulted from the work-recovery cycles and heat stress.
